title: Merge Sorted
statement: Implement `solve(rows)`. `rows` is a list of lists, each sorted ascending. Merge them into one sorted list. Empty rows contribute nothing. A heap of the current head of each row is enough.
constraints: The merge is stable with respect to values. Equal values may come from any row.
hints: Push (value, row_index, index_in_row) for each non-empty row.
Pop the smallest, append it, and push the next value from that same row if one exists.
The row index in the tuple breaks ties so the heap never compares two lists.

approaches.name: Heap of heads
approaches.explanation: A heap of k heads merges the rows in O(n log k).

editorial: A heap of k heads merges the rows in O(n log k). Concatenate-and-sort also works and ignores the fact that the rows are already sorted. The index in the heap tuple matters: without it, equal integers are fine, but you must not let the heap fall through to comparing the rest of a row.
